g. Parks and Recreation Areas:
Byrd Park and Maymont Park comprise the western border of the Randolph Project Area and are two major parks and recreational areas for the city. Byrd Park consists of 300 acres and offers a full range of activities including 12 tennis courts, picnic areas, and football and baseball fields. Maymont Park consists of 94 acres and offers active and passive recreation areas in addition to the Maymont-Virginia Wildlife Exhibit and the Maymont Nature Center. All of the four schools located in the Project Area have playgrounds and equipment. The Clark Springs School is in addition adjacent to the Horace Edwards Recreation Area consisting of approximately four acres and two baseball fields. The Randolph School grounds are adjacent to the Randolph swimming pool, one of the six permanent pools located in the city. It should be noted that Byrd Park, Maymont Park, and Horace Edwards Recreation Area are scheduled and used by organized teams from throughout the city. The school playgrounds and the Randolph Pool are usually used by Randolph Project residents.
The plan will provide for more open space and recreational facilities than exists today. Again, it should be mentioned that this increase in recreational areas will not be accompanied by a significant increase in the Randolph population. Therefore, it is anticipated that the program will result in an overall gain in this regard.
2. Character of the Community:
a. Of the 9,000 persons living in the Randolph Community 98 percent are black. Approximately 34 percent of the population is under 18 years old, while 12 percent is over 62 years. There are 1,086 homeowners, 1,679 renters, and 183 roomers or boarders.
The mean family income in 1969 was $7,226. Of the 2,014 families reported 794 (39%) had incomes less than $5,000; while 487 (24%) had incomes over $10,000. Census tract 413 (everything east of Meadow Street) had the greater percentage of lowest incomes and the smallest percentage of highest incomes.
